stories.title: Don't anthropomorphize big tech companies
stories.summary: Bryan Cantrill has a great line from a talk where he cautions against anthropomorphizing1 Oracle CEO Larry Ellison. I think it’s also a mistake to treat any tech company like a person. Here’s the full quote: You need to think of Larry Ellison the way you think of a lawnmower. You don’t anthropomorphize your lawnmower, the lawnmower just mows the lawn, you stick your hand in there and it’ll chop it off, the end.

stories.title: Google Optimizes Agent Development Kit's 200K-line Python Codebase Overnight with Gemini 4 Argon

stories.title: OpenAI offers discounts up to 90 percent to poach Anthropic's biggest customers
stories.summary: OpenAI is poaching Anthropic's customers with steep discounts. Companies like Rippling, Replit, and DataCamp say they've cut AI costs by up to 90 percent after switching. Anthropic's growth has slowed, but OpenAI is trading its own margins for market share. Chinese rivals like Deepseek are piling on more price pressure.

stories.title: Anthropic says one AI agent beats many subagents now that models can handle complexity alone
stories.summary: Anthropic says companies should evaluate whether they can consolidate sub-agents into a single agent that loads context on demand. In one architecture comparison, the single-agent setup ran about twice as fast. Anthropic has published a migration kit on GitHub to help teams make the transition.

stories.title: Ex-Google CEO Eric Schmidt calls OpenAI and Anthropic modern colonial trading companies
stories.summary: In Foreign Affairs, historian Niall Ferguson, researcher Lisa Klaassen, and former Google CEO Eric Schmidt cast the US and China as AI empires and every other country as a dependency. The race won't be decided by breakthroughs but by who can bankroll it. US corporations alone plan to spend more than $600 billion in 2026.

stories.summary: A new benchmark by P-Zero Research measures how well AI models design and evaluate experiments on their own. The results are improving so fast that Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark now thinks self-improving AI could arrive by 2027.

stories.title: Argus – a free, open-source agentic security operations platform – MIT
OpenAI's isolated AI agents found ways to talk to each other through CPU cache
stories.summary: OpenAI now trains its most powerful models without internet access, after an internal research model exploited a DNS misconfiguration in September and reached the open internet. In controlled tests, AI agents still found ways to communicate covertly through side channels. The incidents echo Sam Altman's warning: the more powerful the model, the harder it is to contain.

stories.title: Three fired OpenAI safety researchers say they were never told what they actually leaked
stories.summary: The three OpenAI safety researchers who were fired, Tomek Korbak, Mikita Balesni, and Jasmine Wang, are publicly pushing back against allegations from their former employer. They deny sharing confidential information and see a connection to their advocacy for AI systems that are easier to scrutinize. The researchers say OpenAI never told them in writing which information they allegedly mishandled.
